learningObjectives.title: Reactivity series and extraction of metals

questions.q: In the reactivity series, which of these metals is the most reactive?
questions.explain: Potassium sits near the top of the reactivity series, making it far more reactive than iron, zinc or copper.

questions.q: Metals that are less reactive than carbon are usually extracted from their ores by:
questions.explain: Carbon can remove oxygen from the oxides of metals less reactive than itself, so those metals are extracted by reduction with carbon.

questions.q: Aluminium is extracted by electrolysis rather than by heating with carbon because aluminium is:
questions.explain: Carbon cannot reduce the oxides of metals more reactive than itself, so more reactive aluminium must be extracted by electrolysis.

questions.q: In terms of oxygen, oxidation is defined as:
questions.explain: Oxidation is the gain of oxygen, while reduction is the loss of oxygen.

questions.q: In terms of electrons, reduction is:
questions.explain: Using OIL RIG, Reduction Is Gain of electrons.

questions.q: In the reaction: iron(III) oxide + carbon → iron + carbon dioxide, the iron(III) oxide has been:
questions.explain: The iron oxide loses its oxygen to carbon, so the iron oxide is reduced (and the carbon is oxidised).

questions.q: Which metal is so unreactive that it is found in the Earth as the uncombined element (native metal)?
questions.explain: Gold is very unreactive, so it does not readily form compounds and is found native in the Earth.

questions.q: Gold can be found as the native metal mainly because it:
questions.explain: Its low reactivity means gold does not combine with other elements, so it occurs as the free metal.

questions.q: Phytoextraction (phytomining) is a biological method of extracting metals that uses:
questions.explain: In phytoextraction, plants absorb metal compounds from the soil and are then burned to concentrate the metal in the ash.

questions.q: Bioleaching extracts metals such as copper by using:
questions.explain: Bioleaching uses bacteria to produce leachate solutions that contain metal compounds.

questions.q: One advantage of using phytoextraction and bioleaching is that they:
options: Allow metals to be extracted from low-grade ores
Are always faster than traditional mining
questions.explain: These biological methods can extract metals from low-grade ores that would be uneconomic to mine and smelt traditionally.

questions.q: Which symbol is used to represent a reversible reaction?
questions.explain: The ⇌ symbol shows that a reaction can proceed in both the forward and backward directions.

questions.q: At dynamic equilibrium in a closed system:
options: The forward and backward reactions occur at the same rate
Only the forward reaction is occurring
All the reactants have been used up
questions.explain: At dynamic equilibrium the forward and backward reactions continue but at equal rates, so concentrations stay constant.

questions.q: Equilibrium in a reversible reaction can only be reached if the reaction takes place in:
questions.explain: A closed system stops reactants or products escaping, allowing the forward and backward reactions to balance.

questions.q: Heating blue hydrated copper(II) sulfate gives white anhydrous copper(II) sulfate. Adding water to the white solid turns it:
questions.explain: This reversible reaction reforms the hydrated salt, so adding water returns the solid to its blue colour.

questions.q: A more reactive metal displaces a less reactive metal from its compound. Which reaction will take place?
options: Zinc + copper sulfate → zinc sulfate + copper
Copper + zinc sulfate → copper sulfate + zinc
Silver + copper sulfate → silver sulfate + copper
Copper + iron sulfate → copper sulfate + iron
questions.explain: Zinc is more reactive than copper, so it displaces copper from copper sulfate solution.

questions.q: Which statement best describes an ore?
options: A rock containing enough of a metal or its compound to make extraction worthwhile
A sample of a completely pure metal
A type of acid used to dissolve metals
questions.explain: An ore is a rock that contains a metal or metal compound in a high enough concentration to be extracted economically.

questions.q: Extracting reactive metals by electrolysis is expensive mainly because it:
options: Uses large amounts of electrical energy
Cannot be done in a factory
questions.explain: Melting the ore and driving the electrolysis both need large amounts of electrical energy, which is costly.

questions.q: Using the mnemonic 'OIL RIG', oxidation is:
questions.explain: OIL RIG stands for Oxidation Is Loss, Reduction Is Gain of electrons.

questions.q: During electrolysis of molten aluminium oxide, aluminium ions (Al³⁺) gain electrons at the cathode. This means the aluminium ions are:
questions.explain: Gaining electrons is reduction, so the Al³⁺ ions are reduced to aluminium metal at the cathode.
